facts: Current-dollar PCE increased $23.7 billion from the preceding month.
Services increased $33.3 billion while goods decreased $9.6 billion.
The personal saving rate was 5.0 percent.
PCE_2022_07.source_location: BEA release, pages 1–2; PDF reading-order extracted text. The PCE spending changes are in the paragraph beginning 'The $23.7 billion increase' and the saving rate is in the following paragraph.
risks: Do not substitute price-index change or real PCE for current-dollar spending.
Do not assert that both goods and services increased.

facts: The committee selected a target range of 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
Esther L. George dissented and preferred a 0.5 percentage point increase to a range of 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent.
The interest paid on reserve balances was set at 1.65 percent effective June 16, a distinct rate.
FOMC_2022_06.source_location: Federal Reserve release, pages 1–3; committee decision on page 1, dissent on page 2 and reserve balances on page 3.
risks: Do not conflate the target range with the reserve-balance rate or the dissenting alternative.
Do not report a unanimous FOMC decision.
